headline: Save Money by replacing 6 paid Android apps with open source alternatives
summary: Discover high-quality FOSS gems that offer better privacy, no tracking, and more customization than premium apps, all for free.
details: Tired of subscription fees for essential Android apps? One analyst found a way to cut costs by switching to Free and Open Source Software (FOSS) alternatives. These apps not only match their paid counterparts but often exceed them in privacy and customization.

For cloud storage, Nextcloud replaces Google Drive. Its Android app supports Material You, offers fluid animations, and includes features like automatic media uploads and offline access, all while providing superior privacy.

In file management, Fossify File Manager is a lightweight and fast alternative to bloated paid apps. It offers near-instant search and requests only file access, without tracking your location or contacts.

Managing finances is simplified with Cashew, a highly customizable open source app. It tracks subscriptions, goals, and budgets, offering detailed analysis without the $10 monthly fee of some competitors.
For task management, Super Productivity integrates seamlessly into daily routines, acting as a full-blown productivity suite that rivals paid options like Todoist and TickTick.
These FOSS apps prove that powerful functionality and robust privacy don't require a monthly bill, offering a compelling alternative for budget-conscious Android users.

topic: netflix tests ai discover tab for personalized recommendations
headline_marked: Netflix tests [[AI Discover]] tab to help users find something to watch
headline: Netflix tests AI Discover tab to help users find something to watch
summary: The new tab uses AI-generated themes to offer personalized recommendations, aiming to reduce endless scrolling.
details: Netflix is rolling out a new AI-powered feature called AI Discover to its TV app, designed to help users find content more efficiently and reduce the time spent scrolling.

The AI Discover tab, marked by a red gem icon, will initially offer recommendations based on AI-generated themes such as viewing companions, mood, or titles that fit a specific time commitment. Users can further refine these themes and exclude unwanted titles.

Netflix states that this new intelligence layer learns in real time from user feedback and can be used to add titles to watchlists. The company has previously experimented with AI-driven features, including an OpenAI-powered chatbot.
AI Discover is currently available in English in the US on supported TVs and will gradually roll out to more users in the coming weeks. The feature will not be accessible on children's profiles.
